title: Copy Any Clearance: CRAFT
hook: ATC talks at 200 words a minute. Here's how you win.

scenes.narration: Alright kid, thirty seconds on the clock. Clearance delivery talks fast. You write faster — because you know what's coming.
Every IFR clearance comes in the same order. C, R, A, F, T. Clearance limit. Route. Altitude. Frequency. Transponder. The FAA loves a good acronym almost as much as I love coffee.
So before you even key the mic, write C R A F T down the page. Now you're not scribbling a mystery novel — you're filling in blanks.
onScreenText: Then just fill in the blanks

scenes.narration: One trap: 'cleared as filed' still comes with an altitude, a frequency, and a squawk. Read it all back. ATC grades on participation.
Clearance limit, route, altitude, frequency, transponder. CRAFT. Learn it cold, kid — it's the one craft project that keeps you out of a mountain.
Don't take my word for it. A I M four dash four dash three. Go read it.

quiz.question: In CRAFT, what does the first C stand for?
quiz.explanation: Every IFR clearance starts with the clearance limit — usually your destination airport. (AIM 4-4-3)

quiz.question: You hear "cleared to Denver as filed." What should you still expect to copy?
quiz.explanation: "As filed" covers the route only. The A, F, and T of CRAFT — altitude, frequency, transponder — are still coming.

quiz.question: Why write C-R-A-F-T on your pad before calling clearance delivery?
choices: Clearances follow that exact order, so you just fill in blanks
ATC will ask you to read the letters back
quiz.explanation: Clearance items are issued in a standard order (AIM 4-4-3). Pre-writing CRAFT turns a fast readback into a fill-in-the-blank.
